name: DPNCA-LM
what: A 12-layer pre-norm transformer skeleton whose attention sublayer is replaced by six iterated steps of a causal 2D neural cellular automaton; the only cross-position operator is a bank of depthwise causal convolutions (0.083% of the model).
scale: 158,881,044 params · 250M Pile tokens · one 19 h run on an RTX 4080 SUPER
measured: Full-validation CE 3.512 nats/token (ppl 33.5) on The Pile, re-measured from the released checkpoint
Same-size GPT-2 at the same token budget: CE 3.346 (ppl 28.4) — the transformer wins by 15–18%
Causality verified bit-exact; zero attention parameters (471/471 tensors match)
Receptive-field ceiling 433 of 1,024 tokens
baseline: GPT-2 162M at 250M tokens from the NCALM harness (different tokenizer; not protocol-identical, but decisive)
verdict: The only attention-free architecture in the portfolio within striking distance of a transformer. Two of its three loss terms never produced a gradient; the reported cross-entropy is cleanly separable from both. Undertrained (1.57 tokens/param) and bounded to a 433-token receptive field by construction. Rebuilt as the whole model (E1), the cellular-automaton rule carries a language model on its own, 0.13 bits/byte ahead of a two-layer transformer at each one's best learning rate; with three times the bytes the transformer catches up.

name: NCALM
family: attention-free · NCA variants vs a matched baseline
what: A model-agnostic training harness with a GPT-2-style baseline (Pythia-160M layout) trained at 250M and 2.0B Pile tokens, and fifteen neural-cellular-automaton variants trained under the same protocol.
scale: 41k lines · 162.3M baseline · 2.0B and 250M Pile tokens · seed 42 · one GPU
measured: GPT-2 baseline: best val PPL 14.45 at 2.0B tokens, 27.57 at 250M
v7.1 (four attention layers + shared conv/GLU loop): 15.68 at 2.0B, behind the baseline at 29 of 30 checkpoints; last-8 mean 17.66 vs 15.16
v13 (gated transformer): 56.98 at 250M · v15 (2D NCA, no attention): 522.5 · v10 (pure NCA): 437.1 (documented only)
baseline: Matched tokens, tokenizer, seed, LR, schedule, effective batch and GPU — the fairest baseline in the portfolio; two eval-protocol defects (random validation windows; larger eval batch for the baseline) both favour the challengers
verdict: The question was sharp and the answer was no: weight-shared local update rules showed no headroom as drop-in replacements for attention at this scale. The harness and baseline are the most reusable artifact in the portfolio. Rebuilt as the whole model (E1 and E5), the shared rule and the v13 morphogen field each carry a language model on their own, 0.13 bits/byte ahead of a two-layer transformer and 0.28 ahead of a one-layer transformer at best rates.

name: WaveLM
what: A byte-level model whose state is a complex field advanced by twelve steps of dilated causal convolution, low-rank channel mixing, a radial saturating nonlinearity, phase rotation and energy normalisation, with a squared-magnitude readout. Mechanically a complex diagonal state-space model.
scale: 7.35M params on The Pile · 0.5M–7M ladder on TinyStories · 40-run ablation campaign
measured: 2.298 bits/byte on The Pile (full validation), 1.355 on TinyStories
Ladder vs a byte transformer at matched DOF: 1.528/1.448/1.364/1.324 vs 1.385/1.093/1.037/0.947 — the transformer wins at every rung
Ablations: saturation removed +0.74 bpb, mixing removed +0.49, real-valued twin +0.20, phase carrier +0.02, Born readout removed −0.03 (better)
baseline: Seeded, DOF-matched byte transformer with a per-architecture LR sweep; depth not matched
verdict: A real language model that loses to its own baseline, with a clean measurement of what drives it: the pointwise nonlinearity, channel mixing and depth. The wave-specific parts add little (the complex field 0.20 bits per byte over its real twin, the phase carrier 0.02, the readout none).

name: HDC-LM
family: backprop-free credit assignment · phasor linear attention
what: A gated linear-attention language model over complex phasors, trained without autograd by equilibrium propagation plus exact eligibility traces (RIPPLE), compared to the identical model trained by BPTT.
scale: 1.13M-param twins on TinyStories · 2-layer MQAR recall · 162M on The Pile
measured: RIPPLE within +3.3% of its BPTT twin at matched data, seed and LR (3.59 vs 3.48 val NLL, 2 seeds); the first-reported 9% was two fixable gradient approximations
MQAR recall: BPTT 1.000 · depth-credit rule 0.998 · no weight transport 0.997 · pure-local 0.261 · no backward pass 0.012
Pile 162M: val PPL 517 vs a 28.9 anchor — the programme's ceiling
baseline: The identical model under BPTT: the cleanest control in the portfolio
verdict: Weight transport is nearly free; reverse-time credit is the wall. The backprop-free rule matched BPTT only where it reproduced BPTT's gradient, and lost everywhere it departed from it.

name: SFNN
what: A grant-proposal-grade plan to run language models on fixed nonlinear optical-fiber propagation steered by a few trainable phase modulators, simulate-first via the GNLSE.
verdict: The strongest unbuilt idea in the portfolio: unbuilt, not disproven. Contains a dispersion sign error that would have to be fixed before the simulation is written.

name: Mamba + DeltaNet with active-inference objectives
what: Small Mamba-SSM + DeltaNet language models on TinyStories with predictive-coding and active-inference auxiliary objectives added in stages (V2 → V11).
measured: V7: val PPL 8.03 on TinyStories (GPT-2 BPE, 82M tokens) — the best honest number in the lineage
A later headline of 5.8 was a metric bug (a precision-weighted score left active at eval); the plain cross-entropy of that checkpoint is 8.69
The active-inference terms were 0.33–0.76% of the loss; learned precision converged to the predicted fixed point without changing perplexity
baseline: No same-tokenizer plain baseline was trained
verdict: The backbone did the work. Without a same-tokenizer plain baseline, the reported perplexities cannot show whether the active-inference objectives helped.

name: APCN-LM / VTM-LM / PROTHEUS
what: Hierarchical predictive-coding cells (diagonal Kalman filters) fused with standard transformer blocks (APCN-LM, ~72% transformer); a discrete active-inference language agent whose ~332M-value phenotype is expanded from a 3.87M-parameter genome and trained by evolutionary search (VTM-LM); ten gradient-free restarts (PROTHEUS).
measured: APCN-LM: documented PPL 28.6 at 250M Pile tokens — the run directory was not retained
Own collapse analysis: KL ≈ 0.004, Kalman gain pinned at its floor, cross-entropy carrying ≥ 93% of the gradient
baseline: No transformer baseline on any branch
verdict: The best numbers have no surviving log and no control. The predictive-coding branch collapsed to a near-no-op, and that collapse was measured carefully. Rebuilt as the whole model (E6), two-level predictive coding carries a language model on its own, 0.36 bits/byte behind a trained GRU at best rates.

name: NEN
what: A dependency-free NumPy hierarchical predictive-coding classifier plus a reward-free contingency-tracking environment.
measured: MNIST 95.31%, Fashion-MNIST 84.6% with clean disjoint splits
The inference-time relaxation contributes nothing measurable; the update is numerically identical to backprop (cosine +1.000000)
baseline: Logistic regression (92.7%); the matched backprop MLP was never run
verdict: Clean engineering, a known algorithm: an MLP trained by a hand-rolled backprop variant.

name: FEDN / CAIN
family: free-energy descent in place of layers
what: Byte-level TinyStories models in which K transformer layers are replaced by K steps of Langevin descent on a learned scalar free energy of a hidden field.
measured: Every version lost to its matched byte-transformer baseline (v3.1: 2.502 vs 1.495 NLL) at ~2% of the compute
K = 1 → 32 descent steps moved NLL by 0.004 nats, non-monotonically
baseline: Matched byte transformers for v2 / v3.1; none for CAIN
verdict: The descent steps change the loss by 0.004 nats and are switched off at inference, leaving an MLP over byte and position embeddings.

name: olento (EDO)
family: self-modifying x86-64 organism · ternary weights as instructions
what: A freestanding static x86-64 binary (C and assembly, no libc) in which learned ternary weights are rendered as live ADD/SUB/NOP instructions and patched in place one opcode byte at a time, with correct i-cache serialisation.
measured: Live .text self-modification verified to the opcode byte
The language model around it never beat a unigram predictor on TinyStories; coverage of the self-modifying path ≤ 0.13% of parameters
verdict: The single most original systems artifact in the portfolio. The self-modifying path covers at most 0.13% of the weights, so learning did not run through it.

name: HARM-LM
family: gradient-free renormalising generative model · VSA context · ridge readout
what: A NumPy-only byte model combining a Dirichlet renormalising generative model with variational message passing, hyperdimensional context codes and a closed-form ridge readout; later versions reverted to backprop-trained transformer blocks.
measured: Best 4.64 bits/byte on TinyStories vs an order-0 byte-frequency floor of 4.45; later runs degraded monotonically with more data
verdict: Three gradient-free implementations, all above the byte-frequency floor; the later versions drifted back to transformer blocks.

name: Wave-AI treatise
what: A ~10,000-word treatise on wave-native computation for AI — leapfrog wave-equation dynamics, the wave↔RNN correspondence, trainability via adjoint methods — and a proposed Wave Computation Network.
verdict: The proposed architecture is original and untested; the document has no reference section and several derivation errors. It seeded HDC-LM two months later.

name: APEIRON
what: A 14.1M-parameter byte model on a sparse random graph (8,192 units, 393K edges) with per-unit time constants and graph synaptogenesis/pruning, documented with pre-registered falsifiable hypotheses.
measured: All runs at or above the 8.0 bits/byte uniform floor; 89.3% of the parameters reached 0.009% of the logits
verdict: A message-scaling bug left the substrate contributing 0.009% of the logits, so the project's own question was never put to a test.

name: DRN
what: A 160M TinyStories model whose ~136M operational weights are emitted by a 418K-parameter hypernetwork over Gray-coded index pairs, applied in a weight-tied depth-recurrence loop.
scale: 3,794 lines · 177 KB design document · 21,504 tokens ever processed
measured: Logged cross-entropy 10.8125 at every step = ln(50257): the model was dead at initialisation (zero-initialised generator output)
verdict: Built and run; training never started because the generator was zero-initialised. The hypernetwork module itself is clean and reusable. Rebuilt as the whole model (E3 and E4): the genome does not carry a language model and finishes worse than its null arm; the coupled oscillators do, 0.31 bits/byte behind a trained GRU at best rates.

name: RGLM lineage
what: Three generations of 'renormalisation-group' language models: per-token bottleneck MLPs with a zero-parameter free-energy attention; a count-table hierarchy; a 163M weight-shared excitatory/inhibitory kernel with a three-level hierarchy.
measured: Trained prototypes stayed at unigram-level perplexity (CE 6.34 nats ≈ ppl 566) and no baseline comparison was run
verdict: Three generations; in each, the hierarchy never reached the gradient. The one genuine novelty (a VQ-VAE block-spin coarse-graining operator) was deprecated hours after it was written and never run.

name: Chaotic Reservoir LM
family: frozen reservoir · reproduction of Liu et al. 2024
what: A 78M-parameter model with a frozen sparse 'chaotic' reservoir between a trainable input projection and a trainable output head, trained for 27 days on 8.3B tokens.
scale: 78,034,855 params · 8.3B tokens (padding counted) · 27 days on one GPU
measured: Final training CE 5.25 nats (ppl 190.7); a power-law fit of its own curve gave an asymptote of 5.12 nats (R² 0.998)

With spectral radius 2.1 the nonlinear branch is unreachable and the sequence axis is flattened into the batch, so the trained model is a rank-512 factorisation of a bigram table — about 0.26 nats worse than a count-based bigram at matched data
verdict: As built, the reservoir added nothing beyond a rank-512 bigram table. The 27-day streaming/resume training infrastructure is the transferable part. Rebuilt as the whole model (E2), a fixed random reservoir that recurs carries a language model on its own, 0.20 bits/byte behind a trained GRU at best rates.

name: developmental-lm
what: Six pre-registered attempts to make a compact genome load-bearing in a small language model (SOMA, GNOMON, ANLAGE, PALIMPSEST, SPORE, TEMPO), each with kill criteria written before the run, plus a replication of the PNAS genomic bottleneck on a 13M LM and a mechanism-screening harness.
scale: 67k lines · 207 commits in 13 days · models ≤ 78M · TinyStories
measured: Genomic bottleneck at birth: CE 2.86 / 2.84 (2 seeds) vs null 9.01 and trained 1.86 — embeddings exempt, so 5.9× overall compression, 107× on the compressed layers
Transfer to a never-seen task family: copied weights +1.33 nats worse than a random start; the genome decode +0.007
Under environment shift, copying weights (4.08) beats every compressed rebirth (4.32–4.70); replay 1.98, generative rehearsal 2.13, EWC 3.36, LwF 3.19
SPORE, a backprop-free HDC LM: 2.41 nats at 25M tokens vs trigram 3.17 (a 13M transformer: 1.86)
GNOMON's evolved elite at 5.24 nats vs a free-weight twin of the same architecture at 3.02
baseline: Matched token budgets, paired seeds, common random numbers; the FLOP-matched copy control in PALIMPSEST was not run
verdict: Every compact-genome mechanism lost to copying weights at matched compute, and each loss was called by a criterion written before the run. Where compression does help is transfer, not stationarity.
note: Not part of the August audit; reviewed independently in October 2026.

name: FlyBrain-LLM
family: connectome-derived principles for sequence memory · pre-registered
what: Does the fruit-fly connectome (MaleCNS v1.0) contain computational principles that improve sequence-memory layers? Identified circuits are verified against published wiring, their principles re-implemented as differentiable modules (a sparse winner-take-all address from the mushroom body; per-address history states), and tested against tuned baselines with hash-locked pre-registrations, frozen verdict rules and the full control set.
scale: three phases · 124 tests · 100-run and 95-run GPU grids, 5 seeds per arm, on one RTX 4080 SUPER
measured: Module level (E1): a fixed random sparse code recalls 0.993 of 128 stored pairs where dense keys recall 0.368 at equal active rows; replicated on fresh seeds

In a trained model (rung 1b): the Kenyon-cell address recalls 0.9995 / 0.9993 / 0.9972 at 32 / 64 / 128 pairs where Gated DeltaNet with 16-d keys recalls 0.79 / 0.81 / 0.79; higher at all 15 seed pairs; verdict under the frozen rule: FALSIFIED (above two seed-spreads at one of three settings, not two)

Controls: an equal-memory dense key 1.000, product keys 0.999, a learned expansion 1.000, the expansion without sparsity 0.810: the win is capacity, not the fly's wiring; the exact sparse step is slower on the GPU (44 vs 21 ms)

History states in a trained model (rung 1): +0.016 and +0.006 over the identical model without them (0.3 seed-spreads); a single store with the same memory ahead by 0.040 and 0.094; FALSIFIED on every conjunct
Language-model test (rung 2) not run: its rules reserved it for a supported mechanism; exploratory 34M WikiText-103 runs show the memory is not what recalls far facts
baseline: Gated DeltaNet at equal active rows and parameters, plus equal-compute, equal-memory, product-key and learned-expansion controls; hash-locked pre-registrations recorded in every run; code identity checked across each grid
verdict: Two hypotheses, both falsified by rules written before the runs, with the controls saying why: the sparse address is a real capacity mechanism but neither fly-specific nor cheaper on a GPU, and the history states' small module-level gain vanished in a trained model. The standard, applied from day one.
note: After the audit; not scored. Reviewed in October 2026: every headline number recomputes from the per-run tables, and the pre-registration hash in every run matches the locked file.
